comparator.description: Every number marker is compared with its complete careful-English meaning, including the material nonclaims.

examples.english: Case 700000: Amina briefed the curators beside the satellite pointing table; either antecedent remains a live subject of the next clause. The pronoun denotes exactly one actor, without specifying gender or identity; that one actor published record 700000. This does not say every curator acted or that anyone acted collectively.
examples.ainglish: Case 700000: Amina briefed the curators beside the satellite pointing table; either antecedent remains a live subject of the next clause. they-one published record 700000.
examples.question: How many actors does the subject pronoun denote?

comparator.description: Both arms are embedded in the same immutable coordination-record frame. English states the complete registered mapping and exclusions; Ainglish changes only that mapping to the compact marker.

example.english: In immutable coordination packet Sep04-they-number-41, the operative record says: The report discusses the auditor and the release team. Exactly one entity—the first antecedent—approved build Cedar; no all-member claim is made.
example.ainglish: In immutable coordination packet Sep04-they-number-41, the operative record says: The report discusses the auditor and the release team. they-one approved build Cedar.
example.question: For packet Sep04-they-number-41, did exactly one referent or two-or-more referents perform the action, and does the sentence alone assert that every member of the salient group acted?

example.english: The auditor spoke with the release committee after the test. Exactly one person or entity approved the rollout.
example.ainglish: The auditor spoke with the release committee after the test. they-one approved the rollout.
example.question: How many people approved?

nemo.problem: Both real questions ask people-count, while both arms permit entity-denotation. In r1 the committee can be one entity containing several people. The gold exactly one does not follow. Direct cardinality labelling also violates the held-out-consequence rule.
